authoredSolutions.1: Each of the first two NAND gates has both inputs tied together, so it acts as an inverter, producing \(\bar{A}\) and \(\bar{B}\). The third NAND gives \((\bar{A}\cdot\bar{B})' = A+B\) (De Morgan), and the final NAND (again an inverter) gives \((A+B)'\). So \(Y=(A+B)'\) — a NOR gate. Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.7: For a charge accelerated through a potential \(V\), \(\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}\). The electron and proton carry the same charge and are accelerated through the same \(V\), so \(V\) cancels and \(\frac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_p}=\sqrt{\frac{m_p}{m_e}}=\sqrt{\frac{1.00727}{0.00055}}\approx\sqrt{1831}\approx 43\). Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.9: Number of atoms \(N=\frac{1.5\times10^{-3}}{198}\times 6\times10^{23}=4.55\times10^{18}\). Decay constant \(\lambda=\frac{0.693}{2.7\times24\times3600}=2.97\times10^{-6}\ s^{-1}\). Activity \(=\lambda N=1.35\times10^{13}\ Bq=\frac{1.35\times10^{13}}{3.7\times10^{10}}\approx 357\ Ci\). Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.15: Statement I: the maximum safe speed on the unbanked road is \(v_{max}=\sqrt{\mu g r}=\sqrt{0.2\times9.8\times2}=1.97\ m/s\); the cyclist's \(7\ km/h=1.94\ m/s<1.97\), so he does not slip — I is true. Statement II: on a road banked at \(45^\circ\) with the same friction, \(v_{max}=\sqrt{rg\,\frac{\tan\theta+\mu}{1-\mu\tan\theta}}=\sqrt{2\times9.8\times\frac{1.2}{0.8}}=5.42\ m/s\); \(18.5\ km/h=5.14\ m/s<5.42\), so he crosses safely — II is true. Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.32: The ring methyl group is oxidised to a carboxylic acid (\(-CH_3\to -COOH\)), turning 3-methoxytoluene into 3-methoxybenzoic acid. Such side-chain oxidation is achieved with alkaline \(KMnO_4\) followed by acidification. \(NaBH_4\) and \(LiAlH_4\) are reducing agents and \(HCl/Zn\text{-}Hg\) is a reduction, so none of those work. Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.39: Statement I is false: \(NaH\) is an ionic hydride and a strong reducing agent (a hydride donor), not an oxidising agent. Statement II is true: the lone pair on the nitrogen of pyridine is available for donation, which makes pyridine basic. Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.40: \(C_{60}\) (buckminsterfullerene) is built from 20 six-membered rings and 12 five-membered rings, every carbon being \(sp^2\) with three sigma bonds; the six-membered rings fuse to both ring sizes while each five-membered ring fuses only to six-membered rings. The claim that it contains 12 six-membered and 24 five-membered rings is therefore incorrect. Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.43: A bright silver mirror with ammoniacal \(AgNO_3\) (Tollens' test) shows that product A reduces \(Ag^+\) — characteristic of formic acid (\(HCOOH\)), which retains a \(-CHO\)-type group. Oxidative ozonolysis of the terminal alkyne 1-butyne, \(HC\equiv C-CH_2CH_3\), cleaves it to formic acid and propanoic acid; the formic acid gives the silver mirror. So X is 1-butyne. Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.44: Basicity falls as the nitrogen lone pair is delocalised onto electron-withdrawing acyl groups. \((CH_3CO)_2\overset{..}{N}H\) has its lone pair tied up by two carbonyl groups (an imide-type nitrogen) and is far less basic than the dialkyl/trialkyl amine choices, so it is the least basic. Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.50: Phenylmagnesium bromide (1 equivalent) adds to the most electrophilic group, the nitrile \(-C\equiv N\), giving a magnesium ketimine salt; acidic hydrolysis (\(H_3O^+\)) then converts it to a ketone \(-C(=O)C_6H_5\). The methoxy (\(-OCH_3\)) group is untouched. So X is the aryl phenyl ketone bearing the intact \(-CH(OCH_3)CH_3\) side chain. Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.79: With \(y=vx\), \(2xy\,y'=y^2-x^2\) integrates to \(C_1: x^2+y^2-2x=0\) (a unit circle centred at \((1,0)\)) through \((1,1)\); similarly \(y'=\frac{2xy}{x^2-y^2}\) gives \(C_2: x^2+y^2-2y=0\) (unit circle centred at \((0,1)\)). The circles meet at \((0,0)\) and \((1,1)\), and the enclosed lens area is \(2\int_0^1\left(\sqrt{2x-x^2}-x\right)dx=\frac{\pi}{2}-1\). Hence option (B).
